# Results — Study 315 (Sovereign-Downgrade) on real SPY total-return tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). A directional abnormal-return
event study around the **three** times a major agency cut the US long-term sovereign rating
one notch from the top: S&P (Aug 5, 2011), Fitch (Aug 1, 2023), Moody's (May 16, 2025). All
three were announced **after the US equity close**, so the first tradeable session is the
next business day (the canonical `lag=1` event bar). Returns are SPY **total return**
(dividends reinvested); abnormal = realized minus the sample mean daily return
(constant-mean-return market model — three events leave no room to fit a beta). Raced
against a **synthetic control** of 3,000 random non-event windows on the same tape. As-of
**2026-06-12**; match the fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tape.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Mode | Window | Days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|--:|---|
| SPY | total return | 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-12 | 8,400 | `eb1569cc9e97` |

## The three events — per-event abnormal returns

The first *tradeable* reaction (`lag=1` event bar, the session after each post-close
announcement):

| Event | Tradeable bar | Event-bar abn ret | CAR(0,+1) | CAR(0,+5) | CAR(0,+20) |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **2011 S&P (AAA→AA+)** | 2011-08-08 | **−6.77%** | −2.27% | +0.20% | −3.46% |
| **2023 Fitch (AAA→AA+)** | 2023-08-02 | −1.44% | −1.77% | −2.62% | −2.06% |
| **2025 Moody's (Aaa→Aa1)** | 2025-05-19 | +0.07% | −0.31% | −0.76% | −0.30% |

The headline is a **one-event story**: the famous −6.8% Monday after S&P's Friday-night 2011
cut dwarfs everything. Fitch 2023 was a mild down day; the Moody's 2025 cut was a **non-event**
(stocks finished flat-to-up the next session).

## The naive t-stat vs the honest test

| Window (lag=1) | n | mean CAR | hit-rate | HAC *t* | synthetic-control mean | permutation *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| CAR(0,+1) | 3 | **−1.45%** | 0% | −3.09 | −0.02% | **0.106** |
| CAR(0,+5) | 3 | −1.06% | 33% | −2.45 | +0.00% | **0.427** |
| CAR(0,+20) | 3 | −1.94% | 0% | −2.60 | −0.10% | **0.450** |

The HAC *t* "clears" the bar on the short windows — but **with n = 3 the per-event *t* is
not meaningful**: it is dominated by one observation and a tiny standard error from three
points. The honest test is the **permutation p-value against the synthetic control**, and it
says these windows are **not distinguishable from random dates** (p = 0.11 at one day, p ≈
0.43–0.45 thereafter). A block-bootstrap CI on the event-bar abnormal return is
**[−5.00%, −0.43%]** — wide, and pulled entirely by 2011.

## "Sell the downgrade" — the trade

Go **short** SPY at the first-tradeable bar's close, hold for the window. Costs one-way ×
NAV on the two fills; a short pays borrow each session.

| Hold | gross mean | net mean (2 bp cost, 1 bp/day borrow) | hit-rate | per-event (gross) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--|
| 5 sessions | **−1.86%** | **−1.95%** | 67% | [−7.18%, +0.98%, +0.62%] |
| 20 sessions | −1.59% | −1.83% | 0% | [−4.13%, −0.20%, −0.45%] |

The trade **loses money** — even gross, even before borrow. The reason is the timing trap:
the −6.8% crash *is* the first tradeable bar (the 2011 reaction was a single Monday gap), so
you cannot get short before it; entering at that bar's close shorts the bottom and rides the
rebound. For 2023 and 2025 the short just bleeds the **+10.8%/yr** drift it is fighting. The
only window in which the short "wins" (+2.0% at hold=5) is the **look-ahead** `lag=0` version
— shorting at the announcement-day close *before* the post-close news, which is untradeable
by construction.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is a faithful detector

On a deterministic synthetic SPY tape the same engine recovers a planted announcement-day
dip **only when one is really there**, and finds nothing in the null:

| Planted dip | event CAR(0,+1) | diff vs control | HAC *t* | permutation *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.00 (null) | −0.05% | −0.11% | −0.20 | 0.640 |
| 0.02 | −2.03% | −2.10% | −7.46 | <0.001 |
| 0.04 | −4.02% | −4.08% | −14.73 | <0.001 |
| 0.08 | −7.98% | −8.04% | −29.25 | <0.001 |

The harness banks a planted signal and rejects the null — so the real-tape "nothing" is a
statement about the **data** (three events, one of which carried a real shock that you could
not trade), not a broken pipeline. A synthetic control can never certify a Signal stamp; it
only proves the detector works.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The 2011 reaction was real and large (−6.8% on the first tradeable
  bar), but it is **one event**. Across all three downgrades the CAR is indistinguishable
  from random non-event windows (permutation p = 0.11 at one day, ≈ 0.45 over a month); the
  naive HAC *t* < −2 is an artefact of n = 3. Literature on sovereign-downgrade
  announcement effects exists, but **this tape cannot certify it** — that is exactly the
  inference bar's definition of WEAK.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** "Sell the downgrade" loses money gross and net at every horizon:
  the one big move was an untradeable post-close gap, and shorting after it bleeds the
  market's upward drift plus borrow. The only profitable version requires look-ahead.
- **Sell the downgrade? — BUSTED.** A single Monday in August 2011 is the entire myth; by
  the time anyone could act on the news the drop was already in the tape, and the next two
  downgrades barely registered.
